Programmatic hash comparison confirms identical keys, bare lean_names, frozen one-line Lean types, dependencies, statements, titles and key steps across decomposition-v1..v4.json, and identical natural proofs in v3 and v4. Why split. The supplied proof contains three independent geometric obligations: step 1 (tilt), step 2 (re-graphing) and steps 3-6(c) (patching). It also uses two linear-algebra Notation facts throughout. The run implements one theorem per node with no helper declarations, so a single declaration would be about 900 Lean lines. (2) rotated_coords: graphPoint = E^{-1}, Pythagoras, and infDist(q0(graphPoint a b), T0) = |b|. These are the P_0/Q_0 Notation facts in coordinates.
(3) tilt_of_slab = step 1.
(4) regraph = step 2: contraction and inverse-derivative argument, slope 1/7, existence and uniqueness clauses.
(5) global_graph = steps 3, 4, 5 and 6(a)-(c).
Children 3, 4 and 5 use only child 2; children 1 and 2 use nothing. The dependencies are acyclic.

How the children prove the selected parent. The parent glue is steps 0, 6(d) and 6(e).

subproblems.title: Operator norm is bounded by the Hilbert-Schmidt norm
subproblems.statement: For all natural numbers m, k and every continuous linear map A from the Euclidean space R^m (Rn m) to R^k (Rn k), the operator norm satisfies ||A|| <= hsNorm A, where hsNorm A = sqrt(sum over i < m of |A e_i|^2) and e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 is the i-th standard basis vector.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ {m k : ℕ} (A : Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k), ‖A‖ ≤ hsNorm A
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 for i < m. By definition hsNorm A = Real.sqrt (hsNormSq A), where hsNormSq A = sum_i |A e_i|^2.
1. hsNorm A >= 0, being a square root. By the characterization of the operator norm (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound, Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Operator/Basic.lean:196), it suffices to prove |A x| <= hsNorm A * |x| for every x in R^m.
2. Fix x and write x_i := x i. In the standard basis, x = sum_i x_i • e_i (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin m) ℝ, sum_repr). By linearity A x = sum_i x_i • A e_i. Since |x_i • A e_i| = |x_i| |A e_i|, the triangle inequality gives |A x| <= sum_i |x_i| |A e_i|.
3. The Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for finite real sums (Real.sum_mul_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt, Mathlib/Analysis/Real/Sqrt.lean:499) gives sum_i |x_i| |A e_i| <= sqrt(sum_i |x_i|^2) * sqrt(sum_i |A e_i|^2).
4. sqrt(sum_i |x_i|^2) = |x| (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/PiL2.lean:145), and sqrt(sum_i |A e_i|^2) = hsNorm A by the definitions of hsNorm and hsNormSq. Hence |A x| <= hsNorm A * |x| after commuting the product. Step 1 then gives ||A|| <= hsNorm A.
5. No case split on m is needed: for m = 0 every sum above is empty, x = 0 and hsNorm A = 0, so each inequality reads 0 <= 0.
proof_key_steps: Reduce to the pointwise bound |A x| <= hsNorm A |x| via ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound
Expand x in the standard basis; triangle inequality gives |A x| <= sum |x_i| |A e_i|
Cauchy-Schwarz for finite real sums
Identify sqrt(sum |x_i|^2) = |x| and sqrt(sum |A e_i|^2) = hsNorm A

subproblems.title: Orthonormal coordinates adapted to the rotated plane q0(R^n x {0})
subproblems.statement:
For all natural numbers n, l:
(i) graphPoint a b = E^{-1}(a, b) for all a in R^n and b in R^l. Here E = EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd : R^{n+l} -> R^n x R^l is Mathlib's canonical continuous linear splitting into the first n and the last l coordinates.
(ii) |graphPoint a b|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2.
(iii) For every linear isometry q0 of R^{n+l} and all a, b, the distance infDist from q0(graphPoint a b) to the n-plane rotatedPlane q0 = q0(R^n x {0}) equals |b|.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), (∀ (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), graphPoint a b = (EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd : Amb n ℓ ≃L[ℝ] Rn n × Rn ℓ).symm (a, b)) ∧ (∀ (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), ‖graphPoint a b‖ ^ 2 = ‖a‖ ^ 2 + ‖b‖ ^ 2) ∧ ∀ (q₀ : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), infDist (q₀ (graphPoint a b)) (rotatedPlane q₀ : Set (Amb n ℓ)) = ‖b‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: E := EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd (Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/PiL2.lean:378). H := horizontalPlane n l = span{EuclideanSpace.single (Fin.castAdd l i) 1 : i < n}.
1. Proof of (i). E is a continuous linear equivalence, hence injective, so it suffices to show E(graphPoint a b) = (a, b). Then graphPoint a b = E^{-1}(E(graphPoint a b)) = E^{-1}(a, b).
By its definition, E is LinearIsometryEquiv.piLpCongrLeft 2 ℝ ℝ finSumFinEquiv.symm followed by EuclideanSpace.sumEquivProd. So for z in R^{n+l}, the first component of E z is i -> z(Fin.castAdd l i) and the second is j -> z(Fin.natAdd n j).
graphPoint a b = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.append a b) has coordinate a_i at castAdd l i (Fin.append_left) and b_j at natAdd n j (Fin.append_right). Comparing both components (ext; simp unfolding graphPoint, finAddEquivProd and sumEquivProd) gives E(graphPoint a b) = (a, b).
2. Consequences of (i). E^{-1} is linear, so:
- graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b' = graphPoint (a - a') (b - b'), since (a, b) - (a', b') = (a - a', b - b');
- graphPoint 0 0 = 0;
- a' -> graphPoint a' 0 = E^{-1}(a', 0) is linear.
3. Proof of (ii). In Euclidean space, |z|^2 = sum over p in Fin (n+l) of |z_p|^2 (EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq). Split the index set Fin (n+l) into its castAdd and natAdd parts (Fin.sum_univ_add) and use the coordinates from step 1: |graphPoint a b|^2 = sum_{i<n} |a_i|^2 + sum_{j<l} |b_j|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2.
4. Proof of (iii), reduction. As sets, rotatedPlane q0 = q0 '' H (Submodule.map_coe; q0.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap has the same underlying function as q0). Since q0 is an isometry, infDist(q0 z, q0 '' H) = infDist(z, H) (Metric.infDist_image). So it suffices to prove infDist(graphPoint a b, H) = |b|.
5. H = {graphPoint a' 0 : a' in R^n}.
(contains) graphPoint a' 0 = sum_i a'_i • single(castAdd l i) 1. Compare coordinates: at castAdd l i both sides equal a'_i, because castAdd is injective; at natAdd n j both are 0, because natAdd n j has value >= n while castAdd l i has value < n. So graphPoint a' 0 is a linear combination of the generators of H, hence lies in H.
(contained) By step 2 the range of a' -> graphPoint a' 0 is a submodule. Comparing coordinates, single(castAdd l i) 1 = graphPoint (single i 1) 0, so every generator lies in this range. By Submodule.span_le, H is contained in the range, i.e. every p in H equals graphPoint a' 0 for some a'.
6. Upper bound. graphPoint a 0 lies in H, so infDist(graphPoint a b, H) <= dist(graphPoint a b, graphPoint a 0) = |graphPoint 0 b| by step 2. By (ii), |graphPoint 0 b|^2 = |0|^2 + |b|^2 = |b|^2, and both norms are nonnegative, so |graphPoint 0 b| = |b|.
7. Lower bound. H is nonempty since 0 is in H. Any p in H has the form graphPoint a' 0 (step 5), and dist(graphPoint a b, p) = |graphPoint (a - a') b| by step 2. By (ii), |graphPoint (a - a') b|^2 = |a - a'|^2 + |b|^2 >= |b|^2, so dist(graphPoint a b, p) >= |b|. Metric.le_infDist (Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/HausdorffDistance.lean:508) gives |b| <= infDist(graphPoint a b, H).
8. Steps 6 and 7 give infDist(graphPoint a b, H) = |b|, and step 4 gives (iii).
proof_key_steps: E(graphPoint a b) = (a, b) componentwise (Fin.append_left/right), so graphPoint = E^{-1} and is linear in the pair
Pythagoras: split the Euclidean sum over Fin (n+l) with Fin.sum_univ_add
rotatedPlane q0 = q0 '' horizontalPlane, and infDist is isometry-invariant
horizontalPlane = {graphPoint a' 0}
infDist(graphPoint a b, horizontalPlane) = |b|: upper bound attained at graphPoint a 0, lower bound by Pythagoras

subproblems.title: A small-slope graph lying in a slab around T0 is nearly parallel to T0
subproblems.statement:
Let q, q0 be linear isometries of R^{n+l}, T0 := rotatedPlane q0 = q0(R^n x {0}), v : R^n -> R^l, y in R^{n+l}, s > 0, and eps, h real. Assume:
- |v x1 - v x2| <= eps |x1 - x2| for all x1, x2 in the closed ball B_s(0) of R^n;
- infDist(y + q(graphPoint x (v x)), T0) <= h for every x in B_s(0).
Then infDist(q(graphPoint e 0), T0) <= (h/s + eps) |e| for every e in R^n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} (q q₀ : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (v : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (y : Amb n ℓ) (s ε h : ℝ), 0 < s → (∀ x₁ ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) s, ∀ x₂ ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) s, ‖v x₁ - v x₂‖ ≤ ε * ‖x₁ - x₂‖) → (∀ x ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) s, infDist (y + q (graphPoint x (v x))) (rotatedPlane q₀ : Set (Amb n ℓ)) ≤ h) → ∀ e : Rn n, infDist (q (graphPoint e 0)) (rotatedPlane q₀ : Set (Amb n ℓ)) ≤ (h / s + ε) * ‖e‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: T0 := rotatedPlane q0, E := EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd, B_s(0) is the closed ball in R^n. The sibling arp_rotatedPlane_graphPoint_coords n l supplies:
- (i) graphPoint a b = E^{-1}(a, b);
- (ii) |graphPoint a b|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2;
- (iii) infDist(q0(graphPoint a b), T0) = |b|.
0. Vertical coordinate. For z in R^{n+l} let sigma z := (E(q0^{-1} z)).2. sigma is continuous linear: it composes q0^{-1}, E and the second projection.
By (i) and E^{-1} E = id, z = q0(graphPoint (E(q0^{-1} z)).1 (sigma z)). So by (iii), infDist(z, T0) = |sigma z| for every z.
Since 0 is in T0, |sigma z| = infDist(z, T0) <= dist(z, 0) = |z| (Metric.infDist_le_dist_of_mem).
By (i), graphPoint is linear in the pair (a, b), since E^{-1} is linear. By (ii), |graphPoint 0 b| = |b|.
1. Case e = 0. graphPoint 0 0 = E^{-1}(0, 0) = 0, so q(graphPoint 0 0) = 0. Then infDist(0, T0) = |sigma 0| = 0 = (h/s + eps) |0|.
2. Case e != 0. Put t := s/|e| > 0, x+ := t e and x- := (-t) e. Then |x+| = |x-| = t |e| = s, so x+, x- lie in B_s(0), and x+ - x- = (2t) e.
3. Identity. By linearity of graphPoint and of q:
q(graphPoint ((2t) e) 0) = [y + q(graphPoint x+ (v x+))] - [y + q(graphPoint x- (v x-))] - q(graphPoint 0 (v x+ - v x-)).
This holds because graphPoint x+ (v x+) - graphPoint x- (v x-) = graphPoint (x+ - x-) (v x+ - v x-) = graphPoint ((2t) e) 0 + graphPoint 0 (v x+ - v x-).
4. Estimate. Apply sigma (linear) and the triangle inequality:
|sigma(q(graphPoint ((2t) e) 0))| <= |sigma(y + q(graphPoint x+ (v x+)))| + |sigma(y + q(graphPoint x- (v x-)))| + |sigma(q(graphPoint 0 (v x+ - v x-)))|.
By step 0 the first two terms are infDists to T0 of slab points, so each is <= h by the slab hypothesis at x+ and x-.
The third term is <= |q(graphPoint 0 (v x+ - v x-))| = |graphPoint 0 (v x+ - v x-)| = |v x+ - v x-|, by step 0 and because q is an isometry.
By the Lipschitz hypothesis, |v x+ - v x-| <= eps |x+ - x-| = eps * 2t|e| = 2 eps s.
Hence |sigma(q(graphPoint ((2t) e) 0))| <= 2h + 2 eps s.
5. By linearity, graphPoint ((2t) e) 0 = (2t) • graphPoint e 0, so sigma(q(graphPoint ((2t) e) 0)) = (2t) • sigma(q(graphPoint e 0)). Hence 2t |sigma(q(graphPoint e 0))| <= 2h + 2 eps s. Dividing by 2t = 2s/|e| > 0 gives |sigma(q(graphPoint e 0))| <= (h + eps s)|e|/s = (h/s + eps)|e|.
6. By step 0, infDist(q(graphPoint e 0), T0) = |sigma(q(graphPoint e 0))| <= (h/s + eps)|e|.
proof_key_steps: Vertical coordinate sigma(z) = (E(q0^{-1} z)).2 is linear with infDist(z, T0) = |sigma z| <= |z|
Trivial case e = 0
Test the slab at x+- = +-(s/|e|) e, both in B_s(0)
Linear identity: q(graphPoint(2te, 0)) = difference of slab points minus q(graphPoint(0, v x+ - v x-))
Triangle inequality and the Lipschitz bound give 2t |sigma(q(graphPoint e 0))| <= 2h + 2 eps s; divide by 2t

subproblems.title: Re-graphing a small-slope C^1 graph over a nearby n-plane T0 (slope <= 1/7)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} (q q₀ : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (v : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (y : Amb n ℓ) (c : Rn n) (d : Rn ℓ) (r ε ϑ : ℝ), 0 < r → 0 ≤ ε → ε ≤ 1 / 24 → 0 ≤ ϑ → ϑ ≤ 1 / 12 → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 v (closedBall 0 r) → v 0 = 0 → (∀ x ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) r, ‖fderivWithin ℝ v (closedBall 0 r) x‖ ≤ ε) → (∀ x : Rn n, infDist (q (graphPoint x 0)) (rotatedPlane q₀ : Set (Amb n ℓ)) ≤ ϑ * ‖x‖) → y = q₀ (graphPoint c d) → ∃ f : Rn n → Rn ℓ, ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f (ball c (r / 2)) ∧ (∀ w ∈ ball c (r / 2), ‖fderiv ℝ f w‖ ≤ 1 / 7) ∧ (∀ w ∈ closedBall c (r / 2), ∃ x ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) r, y + q (graphPoint x (v x)) = q₀ (graphPoint w (f w)) ∧ ‖graphPoint x (v x)‖ ≤ r) ∧ (∀ x ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn n) r, ∀ (w : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), y + q (graphPoint x (v x)) = q₀ (graphPoint w b) → w ∈ closedBall c (r / 2) → b = f w)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: B_s(x) is the closed ball and B°_s(x) the open ball; T0 := rotatedPlane q0; E := EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd. Norms of linear maps are operator norms. The sibling arp_rotatedPlane_graphPoint_coords n l supplies:
- (i) graphPoint a b = E^{-1}(a, b);
- (ii) |graphPoint a b|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2;
- (iii) infDist(q0(graphPoint a b), T0) = |b|.
0. Coordinates. For z in R^{n+l} put pi z := (E(q0^{-1} z)).1 in R^n and sigma z := (E(q0^{-1} z)).2 in R^l. Both are continuous linear maps.
By (i): z = q0(graphPoint (pi z) (sigma z)); pi(q0(graphPoint a b)) = a; sigma(q0(graphPoint a b)) = b.
By (ii) and since q0 is an isometry, |z|^2 = |pi z|^2 + |sigma z|^2, so |pi z| <= |z| and |sigma z| <= |z|.
By (iii), infDist(z, T0) = |sigma z|. Also pi y = c.
By (i), graphPoint is linear in the pair: graphPoint a b = graphPoint a 0 + graphPoint 0 b, graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b' = graphPoint (a - a') (b - b'), and graphPoint 0 0 = 0.
By (ii), |graphPoint a 0| = |a| and |graphPoint 0 b| = |b|.
1. Bounds for v. B_r(0) is convex, v is differentiable on it (it is C^1, and 1 != 0), and |fderivWithin v B_r(0) x| <= eps there. By the mean value inequality (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderivWithin_le, Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/MeanValue.lean:484), |v x1 - v x2| <= eps |x1 - x2| for x1, x2 in B_r(0). Since v(0) = 0, |v x| <= eps |x|.
If x is in B°_r(0), then B_r(0) is a neighbourhood of x (closedBall_mem_nhds_of_mem). So v is C^1 at x, fderiv v x = fderivWithin v B_r(0) x (fderivWithin_of_mem_nhds), and |fderiv v x| <= eps.
2. Linear part. Define continuous linear maps A h := pi(q(graphPoint h 0)) from R^n to R^n and V h := sigma(q(graphPoint h 0)) from R^n to R^l.
By step 0, |A h|^2 + |V h|^2 = |q(graphPoint h 0)|^2 = |h|^2. By the tilt hypothesis, |V h| = infDist(q(graphPoint h 0), T0) <= vartheta |h|.
Since 0 <= vartheta <= 1, (1 - vartheta)^2 <= 1 - vartheta^2. Hence |A h|^2 >= (1 - vartheta^2)|h|^2 >= (1 - vartheta)^2 |h|^2, i.e. |A h| >= (1 - vartheta)|h| >= (11/12)|h|.
So A is injective, and in finite dimension (LinearEquiv.ofInjectiveEndo) it is a linear isomorphism of R^n with |A^{-1} k| <= (12/11)|k| for all k.
3. The chart. Put Psi(x) := y + q(graphPoint x (v x)), Phi(x) := pi(Psi(x)) and g(x) := pi(q(graphPoint 0 (v x))). By step 0, Phi(x) = c + A x + g(x).
For x1, x2 in B_r(0), g(x1) - g(x2) = pi(q(graphPoint 0 (v x1 - v x2))), so |g(x1) - g(x2)| <= |v x1 - v x2| <= eps |x1 - x2|. Also g(0) = 0.
Therefore |Phi(x1) - Phi(x2) - A(x1 - x2)| <= eps |x1 - x2| on B_r(0), and Phi(0) = c.
4. Injectivity estimate. For x1, x2 in B_r(0): |Phi(x1) - Phi(x2)| >= |A(x1 - x2)| - |g(x1) - g(x2)| >= (1 - vartheta - eps)|x1 - x2| >= (7/8)|x1 - x2|, because vartheta + eps <= 1/12 + 1/24 = 1/8.
5. Solving Phi(x) = w. Claim: each w in B_{r/2}(c) equals Phi(x) for some x in B_{3r/5}(0).
Let K := B_{3r/5}(0). It is contained in B_r(0) and is complete. Let F_w(x) := A^{-1}(w - c - g(x)).
For x in K: |F_w(x)| <= (12/11)(|w - c| + |g(x)|) <= (12/11)(r/2 + eps * 3r/5) <= (12/11)(r/2 + r/40) = 63r/110 < 3r/5. So F_w maps K into K.
Also |F_w(x1) - F_w(x2)| = |A^{-1}(g(x2) - g(x1))| <= (12/11) eps |x1 - x2| <= (1/22)|x1 - x2|, so F_w is a contraction of K.
By the Banach fixed point theorem F_w has a fixed point x in K. F_w(x) = x means A x = w - c - g(x), i.e. Phi(x) = w.
[Lean: ContractingWith is not imported by GMT.Ch05.Submission. The in-scope lemma ApproximatesLinearOn.surjOn_closedBall_of_nonlinearRightInverse (Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/InverseFunctionTheorem/ApproximatesLinearOn.lean:143) packages exactly this argument. By step 3, Phi is ApproximatesLinearOn A on B_r(0) with constant eps. Use the nonlinear right inverse A^{-1} with nnnorm 12/11 (step 2), centre 0 and radius 3r/5. The lemma gives Phi(B_{3r/5}(0)) ⊇ B_{(11/12 - eps) 3r/5}(Phi(0)), which contains B_{r/2}(c) because Phi(0) = c and (11/12 - 1/24)(3r/5) = 21r/40 >= r/2.]
For each w in B_{r/2}(c) choose such a point x(w) in B_{3r/5}(0) with Phi(x(w)) = w. For other w set x(w) := 0.
6. Definition of f, and (b). Put f(w) := sigma(Psi(x(w))). For w in B_{r/2}(c), pi(Psi(x(w))) = Phi(x(w)) = w, so by step 0, y + q(graphPoint x(w) (v x(w))) = Psi(x(w)) = q0(graphPoint w (f w)).
Also x(w) lies in B_{3r/5}(0), which is inside B_r(0). Moreover |v x(w)| <= eps |x(w)| <= (1/24)(3r/5) = r/40, and by (ii) |graphPoint x(w) (v x(w))|^2 = |x(w)|^2 + |v x(w)|^2 <= (3r/5)^2 + (r/40)^2 < r^2. So |graphPoint x(w) (v x(w))| <= r, which is (b) with x := x(w).
7. Proof of (c). Let x be in B_r(0), w in B_{r/2}(c) and b in R^l with Psi(x) = q0(graphPoint w b). Applying pi and sigma (step 0) gives Phi(x) = w and sigma(Psi(x)) = b.
Also Phi(x(w)) = w with x(w) in B_r(0). Step 4 gives (7/8)|x - x(w)| <= |Phi(x) - Phi(x(w))| = 0, so x = x(w) and b = sigma(Psi(x(w))) = f(w).
8. Derivatives of the chart. By step 0, Psi(x) = y + q(E^{-1}(x, v x)). v is C^1 on the open ball B°_r(0) (restriction of the hypothesis), so Psi and Phi = pi ∘ Psi are C^1 on B°_r(0). Hence x -> fderiv Psi x and x -> fderiv Phi x are continuous on B°_r(0) (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen).
At x0 in B°_r(0), put Dv := fderiv v x0; then |Dv| <= eps by step 1. The chain rule (HasFDerivAt.prodMk, composition with continuous linear maps) gives DPsi(x0) h = q(graphPoint h (Dv h)) and DPhi(x0) = pi ∘ DPsi(x0).
Thus DPhi(x0) h = A h + pi(q(graphPoint 0 (Dv h))), so |DPhi(x0) h| >= (1 - vartheta)|h| - eps|h| >= (7/8)|h|. Hence DPhi(x0) is an injective endomorphism of R^n, i.e. a continuous linear equivalence L_{x0}, with |L_{x0}^{-1} k| <= (8/7)|k|.
Also sigma(DPsi(x0) h) = V h + sigma(q(graphPoint 0 (Dv h))), so |sigma(DPsi(x0) h)| <= vartheta |h| + eps |h| <= |h|/8.
9. x(.) is Lipschitz. For w1, w2 in B_{r/2}(c), step 4 and Phi(x(wi)) = wi give (7/8)|x(w1) - x(w2)| <= |w1 - w2|. So x(.) is (8/7)-Lipschitz, hence continuous, on B_{r/2}(c), with values in B_{3r/5}(0), which is inside B°_r(0).
10. Derivative of f and the slope bound. Fix w in B°_{r/2}(c) and put x0 := x(w). Three facts hold:
- x(.) is continuous at w (step 9);
- Phi has derivative L_{x0} at x(w) (step 8);
- Phi(x(w')) = w' for all w' in the neighbourhood B°_{r/2}(c) of w.
By the local-left-inverse rule (HasFDerivAt.of_local_left_inverse, Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/OfCompLeft.lean:165), x(.) has derivative L_{x0}^{-1} at w.
By the chain rule, f = sigma ∘ Psi ∘ x(.) has derivative f'(w) := sigma ∘ DPsi(x(w)) ∘ DPhi(x(w))^{-1} at w. By step 8, |f'(w) k| <= (1/8)|DPhi(x(w))^{-1} k| <= (1/8)(8/7)|k| = |k|/7. So |fderiv f w| = |f'(w)| <= 1/7 (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound).
11. f is C^1 on B°_{r/2}(c). The map w -> f'(w) = sigma ∘ fderiv Psi (x(w)) ∘ (fderiv Phi (x(w)))^{-1} is continuous at each w in B°_{r/2}(c), because:
- x(.) is continuous with values in B°_r(0) (step 9);
- fderiv Psi and fderiv Phi are continuous there (step 8);
- inversion is continuous at invertible elements of the complete normed ring of endomorphisms of R^n (NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt, Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Units.lean:183, with Ring.inverse(DPhi(x(w))) = L_{x(w)}^{-1}); alternatively, |P^{-1} - Q^{-1}| = |P^{-1}(Q - P)Q^{-1}| <= (8/7)^2 |P - Q| for P, Q of the form DPhi(x(.));
- a composition of continuous linear maps depends continuously on its factors.
f has derivative f'(w') at every point w' of the open set B°_{r/2}(c). Since f' is continuous at every point of B°_{r/2}(c), it is continuous on B°_{r/2}(c), which is a neighbourhood of w. So f is C^1 at w (contDiffAt_succ_iff_hasFDerivAt with n = 0, Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/ContDiff/Defs.lean:1018, together with contDiffAt_zero, Defs.lean:1129, which asks for continuity of f' on a neighbourhood of w, not just at w). Hence f is C^1 on B°_{r/2}(c), and with step 10 this is (a).
Implementation remark: the child is a single theorem with no new imports, options or helper declarations. ContractingWith and ContDiffAt.to_localInverse are not in scope; the lemmas cited above are. A direct Lean rendering of steps 0-11 compiles in a scratch copy of the pinned project under the default heartbeat limit, using between 100000 and 150000 heartbeats. The condition is that every scalar inequality is closed by linarith with explicit product hints, never by nlinarith. Typical hints are mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right applied to vartheta <= 1/12 or eps <= 1/24 and a norm, mul_nonneg (0 <= 1/8 - vartheta - eps) (norm_nonneg _), and mul_nonneg (mul_nonneg (0 <= vartheta) (0 <= 1 - vartheta)) (sq_nonneg |h|) in step 2. Squared bounds use pow_le_pow_left₀, pow_le_pow_iff_left₀ and pow_left_inj₀. An otherwise identical rendering with about 15 nlinarith calls needs between 200000 and 250000 heartbeats and fails the default limit.
proof_key_steps: Coordinates pi, sigma adapted to T0: z = q0(graphPoint (pi z) (sigma z)), infDist(z, T0) = |sigma z|
Mean value inequality: v is eps-Lipschitz on B_r(0), |fderiv v| <= eps inside
Tilt plus Pythagoras: A h = pi(q(graphPoint h 0)) satisfies |A h| >= (11/12)|h|, so A is invertible with |A^{-1}| <= 12/11
Phi = c + A + g with g eps-Lipschitz; injectivity |Phi x1 - Phi x2| >= (7/8)|x1 - x2| on B_r(0)
Contraction (ApproximatesLinearOn surjectivity) solves Phi(x) = w for w in B_{r/2}(c) with x in B_{3r/5}(0); define f(w) = sigma(Psi(x(w))); (b) and (c) follow
DPhi bounded below by 7/8 and |sigma ∘ DPsi| <= 1/8 on the open ball
x(.) is 8/7-Lipschitz; local-left-inverse rule gives Dx = DPhi^{-1}; |Df| <= (1/8)(8/7) = 1/7
Continuity of w -> sigma ∘ DPsi(x(w)) ∘ DPhi(x(w))^{-1} gives C^1 on the open ball

subproblems.title: Local graphs over T0 inside a thin cone patch into one graph over a disc
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} (S : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (q₀ : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (R A B s t κ L : ℝ), 0 < R → 0 < s → 0 ≤ κ → κ < 1 → R ≤ (1 - κ) * A → A + t ≤ B → s + 2 * κ * A ≤ t → IsClosed (S ∩ closedBall 0 A) → (0 : Amb n ℓ) ∈ S → (∀ z ∈ S ∩ closedBall 0 B, infDist z (rotatedPlane q₀ : Set (Amb n ℓ)) ≤ κ * ‖z‖) → (∀ y ∈ S ∩ closedBall 0 A, ∀ (c : Rn n) (d : Rn ℓ), y = q₀ (graphPoint c d) → ∃ f : Rn n → Rn ℓ, ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f (ball c s) ∧ (∀ w ∈ ball c s, ‖fderiv ℝ f w‖ ≤ L) ∧ (∀ w ∈ ball c s, q₀ (graphPoint w (f w)) ∈ S ∩ closedBall y t) ∧ (∀ w ∈ ball c s, ∀ b : Rn ℓ, q₀ (graphPoint w b) ∈ S ∩ closedBall y t → b = f w)) → ∃ u : Rn n → Rn ℓ, ContDiffOn ℝ 1 u (ball 0 R) ∧ (∀ x ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) R, ‖fderiv ℝ u x‖ ≤ L) ∧ (∀ x ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) R, q₀ (graphPoint x (u x)) ∈ S ∩ ball 0 A) ∧ (∀ x ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) R, ∀ b : Rn ℓ, q₀ (graphPoint x b) ∈ S ∩ closedBall 0 A → b = u x) ∧ S ∩ ball 0 R ⊆ q₀ '' graphOver u (ball 0 R)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: B_r(x) is the closed ball and B°_r(x) the open ball; T0 := rotatedPlane q0; E := EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd. 'The hypothesis at y with (c, d)' means the local-graph hypothesis. The sibling arp_rotatedPlane_graphPoint_coords n l supplies:
- (i) graphPoint a b = E^{-1}(a, b);
- (ii) |graphPoint a b|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2;
- (iii) infDist(q0(graphPoint a b), T0) = |b|.
0. Coordinates and parameters. For z in R^{n+l} let pi z := (E(q0^{-1} z)).1 and sigma z := (E(q0^{-1} z)).2. Both are continuous linear maps.
By (i): z = q0(graphPoint (pi z) (sigma z)); pi(q0(graphPoint a b)) = a; sigma(q0(graphPoint a b)) = b.
By (ii) and since q0 is an isometry, |z|^2 = |pi z|^2 + |sigma z|^2, so |pi z| <= |z| and |z| <= |pi z| + |sigma z|.
By (iii), infDist(z, T0) = |sigma z|.
Parameter facts:
- 1 - kappa > 0;
- A > 0, since otherwise (1 - kappa) A <= 0 < R;
- t >= s + 2 kappa A > 0;
- A <= A + t <= B;
- R <= (1 - kappa) A <= A.
1. The cone in coordinates. For z in S cap B_B(0): |sigma z| <= kappa |z|, so |z| <= |pi z| + kappa |z|, i.e. (1 - kappa)|z| <= |pi z|.
Put K := S cap B_A(0), which is contained in S cap B_B(0). Then |sigma z| <= kappa |z| <= kappa A for every z in K.
2. Distance estimate. If z, y are in K and |pi z - pi y| <= s, then |z - y| <= |pi(z - y)| + |sigma(z - y)| <= s + |sigma z| + |sigma y| <= s + 2 kappa A <= t.
3. pi is injective on K. Let y1, y2 be in K with pi y1 = pi y2 =: c. Since y1 = q0(graphPoint c (sigma y1)), the hypothesis at y1 with d := sigma y1 gives some f. As s > 0, c lies in B°_s(c).
First, y1 is in S cap B_t(y1) because t >= 0, so the uniqueness clause gives sigma y1 = f(c).
Second, step 2 gives |y2 - y1| <= t, so q0(graphPoint c (sigma y2)) = y2 is in S cap B_t(y1), and sigma y2 = f(c).
Thus sigma y1 = sigma y2, and y1 = q0(graphPoint c (sigma y1)) = y2.
4. Compactness. K is closed (hypothesis) and contained in the compact ball B_A(0) of the finite-dimensional space (isCompact_closedBall). So K is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset), and D := pi(K) is compact (IsCompact.image) and closed (IsCompact.isClosed). Also 0 is in K (0 is in S and A >= 0), and pi(0) = 0.
5. U := D cap B°_R(0) is open. Let w0 be in U, with w0 = pi y for some y in K. The hypothesis at y with (c, d) := (w0, sigma y) gives some f.
Let w' be in B°_s(w0) cap B°_R(0) and put x' := q0(graphPoint w' (f w')). By the existence clause, x' is in S cap B_t(y), so |x'| <= |y| + t <= A + t <= B and x' is in S cap B_B(0).
By step 1, (1 - kappa)|x'| <= |pi x'| = |w'| < R <= (1 - kappa) A, so |x'| < A. Hence x' is in K and w' = pi x' is in U.
Thus U contains the open neighbourhood B°_s(w0) cap B°_R(0) of each of its points, so U is open (isOpen_iff_mem_nhds).
6. B°_R(0) is contained in D. B°_R(0) is convex, hence preconnected (Convex.isPreconnected). U is open by step 5. B°_R(0) cap U contains 0 (step 4 and R > 0). Since D is closed, closure(U) cap B°_R(0) ⊆ closure(D) cap B°_R(0) = D cap B°_R(0) = U. By IsPreconnected.subset_of_closure_inter_subset, B°_R(0) ⊆ U ⊆ D.
7. Definition of u. For x in B°_R(0), use step 6 and choice to pick z_x in K with pi z_x = x, and set u(x) := sigma z_x. For x outside B°_R(0) set u(x) := 0. Then for x in B°_R(0), q0(graphPoint x (u x)) = q0(graphPoint (pi z_x) (sigma z_x)) = z_x, which is in K.
8. Uniqueness clause. Let x be in B°_R(0) and b in R^l with q0(graphPoint x b) in S cap B_A(0) = K. This point and z_x both lie in K and have pi-coordinate x, so they are equal by step 3. Applying sigma gives b = sigma z_x = u(x).
9. Membership clause. For x in B°_R(0), z_x is in S cap B_B(0). By step 1, (1 - kappa)|z_x| <= |pi z_x| = |x| < R <= (1 - kappa) A, so |z_x| < A. Hence q0(graphPoint x (u x)) = z_x is in S cap B°_A(0).
10. Reverse inclusion. Let z be in S cap B°_R(0). Since |z| < R <= A, z is in K. Put w := pi z; then |w| <= |z| < R. Since z = q0(graphPoint w (sigma z)) is in K, step 8 gives sigma z = u(w). So z = q0(graphPoint w (u w)) with w in B°_R(0), i.e. z is in q0 '' graphOver u (B°_R(0)).
11. Regularity and slope. Fix x0 in B°_R(0) and put y := z_{x0} = q0(graphPoint x0 (u x0)), which is in K. The hypothesis at y with (c, d) := (x0, u x0) gives f, C^1 on B°_s(x0) with |fderiv f| <= L there.
For w in B°_s(x0) cap B°_R(0): z_w is in K and |pi z_w - pi y| = |w - x0| <= s, so |z_w - y| <= t by step 2. Thus q0(graphPoint w (u w)) = z_w is in S cap B_t(y), and the uniqueness clause gives u(w) = f(w).
So u = f on the open neighbourhood B°_s(x0) cap B°_R(0) of x0. f is C^1 at x0, since it is C^1 on the open ball B°_s(x0), which contains x0. Hence u is C^1 at x0 (ContDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq), and fderiv u x0 = fderiv f x0 (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq), so |fderiv u x0| <= L.
Since x0 was arbitrary, u is C^1 on B°_R(0) (each ContDiffAt gives ContDiffWithinAt) with |fderiv u x| <= L there. Together with steps 8-10, this proves all five conclusions.
proof_key_steps: Coordinates pi, sigma; the cone becomes |sigma z| <= kappa|z|, hence (1 - kappa)|z| <= |pi z| and |sigma| <= kappa A on K = S cap B_A(0)
Distance estimate: points of K with |pi z - pi y| <= s are within t of each other
pi is injective on K, via the uniqueness clause at the centre c
K compact, so D = pi(K) is closed; U = D cap B°_R(0) is open by the existence clause plus the cone bound; connectedness of the disc gives B°_R(0) ⊆ D
Define u by choice; uniqueness, membership and reverse inclusion follow from injectivity and the cone bound
Locally u = f (uniqueness clause plus distance estimate), so u is C^1 with |Du| <= L
